subject: [IRACE-Tuning budget] Is there any way to force IRACE using all the training instances even though the tuning budget is low?

messages.author: a5e1111eb2b1e4c4
messages.subject: [IRACE-Tuning budget] Is there any way to force IRACE using all the training instances even though the tuning budget is low?
parts:
Hi Everyone,

My case: I have 36 training instances and a budget of 300 experiments. I run IRACE and only 12 instances were used (one third of the total amount).

Is there any way to force IRACE using all the training instances even though the tuning budget is low for the amout of provided training instances or should I increase the budget value?

Best wishes,

André

messages.author: 1e8700780c0e6d69
messages.subject: Re: [IRACE-Tuning budget] Is there any way to force IRACE using all the training instances even though the tuning budget is low?
parts:
Hello Andre,

You can force irace to evaluate more instances by adjusting the setting of irace. 
This should be done with caution especially because you have a very small budget.
So I add small explanation here so you can decide:

First, if you can increase the budget I would advise you to always do it. A good budget value 
will depend mostly on the number of parameters you have to configure, irace needs evaluations to 
explore and exploit the parameter space, the bigger the space, the more evaluations are likely to be needed.
Now, increasing the budget will not necessarily increase the number of instances, most probably 
it will, but not much.

If you force irace to evaluate more instances, irace distributes the budget to increase the precision of the 
performance evaluation and thus, you reduce the number of configurations of your algorithm that irace can test. Normally we advice
to force more instances to be evaluated  when the instances are heterogeneous. This means that is not easy to find a 
good configurations for all the instances, so irace needs to focus on evaluate many of them to know what is really good.
On the other hand, if your instances are homogeneous, meaning that best configurations are good for all the instances, 
then is ok to evaluate few instances.

If you are using the last irace version I recommend you to adjust the elitistNewInstances setting (by default 1).
irace will add elitistNewInstances new instances each iteration to the evaluation list. 

Complementary, you can adjust the settings related with the elimination tests: firstTest (default 5) and eachTest (default 1).  
The firstTest option will set the number instances required to apply the first statistical test to eliminate bad 
configurations and eachTest will set the intervals of how many instances are required to apply the elimination 
test after firstTest. 


I hope this can help you let me know if you have more questions.

Bests, 
Leslie.

firstTest = 10

I have only three parameters (real numbers with two decimal places) to tune.

I should wait for the results (if all instances were covered) and observe the  time spent in the whole tuning.

Thank you again.
